data.note:
Reflection: I favored Aurora kinase inhibitors on visually confirmed multinucleation at 1-3uM (e8-e11), over a split 4-way NSC vote with modest similarity. Unblinded as mitoxantrone, annotated DNA replication, this was wrong.

Topoisomerase II inhibition explains the miss: DNA damage signaling after mitoxantrone/etoposide relates directly to DNA replication (PMID:22140093), and topo II-mediated cleavage arrests replication fork progression (PMID:9153414), with topo II as a cancer target class (PMID:42442624). Polyploid/multinucleate phenotypes are not specific to Aurora - DNA replication stress can produce them.

Lesson: require dose-trend + orthogonal readout (DNA-content flow/pH3) before leaving split atlas prior on morphology alone.

reflection.text:
We correctly detected a cytotoxic, nuclear phenotype: density lower vs DMSO at all doses, cell counts falling from 72 to 46-52 to 6 cells at 10uM, and very strong frac_large_nucleus signals (z=+15.0 at 0.3uM, z=+61.1 at 1uM, z=+35.0 at 3uM) with low nuc_solidity and visually confirmed large/multinucleate cells. We also correctly noted atlas support was weak and conflicting, with per-well 1-NN votes split four ways and similarities only 0.32-0.55.

We misread that shared polyploidy-like morphology as Aurora-specific. The microscopist candidates Aurora kinase inhibitors at 1uM and 3uM (e10, e11) plus high act_glcm_contrast and tub_glcm_contrast and rounding drove the 0.42 Aurora hypothesis, but topoisomerase II inhibition by mitoxantrone also produces replication arrest and DNA-damage signaling linked to replication (PMID 22140093, PMID 9153414) via interaction with topoisomerase II-alpha (PMID 27834128), which can mimic large irregular multinucleate nuclei and secondary cytoskeletal contraction.

The dose-response and atlas should have stopped us: frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.40 p=0.6 and frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=-0.20 p=0.8 over 4 wells showed no rising Aurora-like trend, and k-neighbours flipped from Aurora 5/10 to Microtubule stabilizers 8/10. We discounted the 6-cell 10uM well as toxic but still favored a mitotic explanation without testing a DNA-replication hypothesis.

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Approve: Aurora is favoured by multinucleation/polyploidy rising across the informative doses — frac_multinucleate_proxy z=+13.0 at 1 uM and z=+18.7 at 3 uM, with visually confirmed cells containing 3-8 distinct nuclei at both doses (e8-e11), plus strongly irregular/large nuclei. A microtubule stabilizer explains the bright compact tubulin, rounding and atlas similarity, but not this repeated failed-cytokinesis morphology with no increase in mitotic-like fraction; actin changes are plausibly secondary to contraction. The 10 uM well (6 cells) was rightly discounted as toxic/non-informative. Atlas support is conflicting and modest (per-well votes split four ways, similarities ~0.32-0.55), so it does not override the direct phenotype. Two adjacent dose indices corroborate the key effect despite single replicates, and the stated 0.55 is appropriately modest given the stabilizer runner-up.

## Unblinding

Compound: **mitoxantrone** (PubChem CID [4212](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/4212))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: DNA topoisomerase II alpha inhibitor; DNA inhibitor

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: the call was **Aurora kinase inhibitors**, BBBC021 annotates **DNA replication**.

## Reflection

We correctly detected a cytotoxic, nuclear phenotype: density lower vs DMSO at all doses, cell counts falling from 72 to 46-52 to 6 cells at 10uM, and very strong frac_large_nucleus signals (z=+15.0 at 0.3uM, z=+61.1 at 1uM, z=+35.0 at 3uM) with low nuc_solidity and visually confirmed large/multinucleate cells. We also correctly noted atlas support was weak and conflicting, with per-well 1-NN votes split four ways and similarities only 0.32-0.55.

We misread that shared polyploidy-like morphology as Aurora-specific. The microscopist candidates Aurora kinase inhibitors at 1uM and 3uM (e10, e11) plus high act_glcm_contrast and tub_glcm_contrast and rounding drove the 0.42 Aurora hypothesis, but topoisomerase II inhibition by mitoxantrone also produces replication arrest and DNA-damage signaling linked to replication (PMID 22140093, PMID 9153414) via interaction with topoisomerase II-alpha (PMID 27834128), which can mimic large irregular multinucleate nuclei and secondary cytoskeletal contraction.

The dose-response and atlas should have stopped us: frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.40 p=0.6 and frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=-0.20 p=0.8 over 4 wells showed no rising Aurora-like trend, and k-neighbours flipped from Aurora 5/10 to Microtubule stabilizers 8/10. We discounted the 6-cell 10uM well as toxic but still favored a mitotic explanation without testing a DNA-replication hypothesis.

What was right:
- Detected strong nuclear enlargement and irregularity (frac_large_nucleus up to z=+61.1, nuc_solidity z=-29.8 at 1uM) with lower density vs DMSO, consistent with cytotoxic DNA replication stress
- Rightly discounted the 10uM well with only 6 cells and extreme rounding scores as toxic/non-informative
- Recognized atlas support was modest and conflicting with per-well votes split four ways and similarities 0.32-0.55, stating modest 0.55 confidence

What was wrong or missed:
- Misattributed visually confirmed multinucleation/large nuclei at 1-3uM to Aurora cytokinesis failure instead of topoisomerase II inhibitor replication arrest and DNA damage
- Overweighted secondary cytoskeletal features (act_glcm_contrast z up to +26.1, tub_glcm_contrast z up to +34.1, roundness changes) as primary actin/microtubule MOAs
- Ignored negative/non-significant dose_response trends for frac_large_nucleus and frac_multinucleate_proxy that contradicted a rising polyploidy model
- Narrowed to Aurora vs Microtubule stabilizer and never acquired or proposed a DNA-replication test despite unblinded mechanism being DNA topoisomerase II alpha inhibitor / DNA inhibitor

Proposed next experiment: EdU pulse plus DNA-content flow with gamma-H2AX and phospho-histone H3, comparing the unknown to mitoxantrone/etoposide versus an Aurora inhibitor control to test replication arrest/DNA damage versus cytokinesis failure.
